Usage: bb status [options]
Show the current project, thread, environment and server
JSON (--json): {project, thread, childThreads, pendingTodos, pluginsNeedingAttention, dataDir, serverUrl}

Usage: bb guide [topic] [group] [options]
Explain bb: concepts, threads, machines, commands, …

Usage: bb whoami [options]
Show the user this CLI acts as
JSON (--json): {user: {id, name, email, role, hasPassword, disabledAt, …}}

Usage: bb thread spawn [options]
Create a thread and send its first prompt
Aliases: create, new
Options:
  --project <id>              Project ID (required; inside a thread: $BB_PROJECT_ID)
  --title <title>             Thread title
  --prompt <text>             First prompt
  --prompt-file <path>        Read the prompt from a file (- reads stdin)
  --parent-self               Parent the new thread to BB_THREAD_ID
  --parent-thread <id>        Parent thread ID
  --provider <id>             Provider ID (default: the project's remembered choice)
  --model <model>             Model ID
  --reasoning-level <level>   none, low, medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra, …
  --permission-mode <mode>    accept-edits, auto or full
  --environment <id-or-path>  Reuse an environment, or run in a directory
  --new-environment <kind>    worktree, checkout or personal
  --base-branch <ref>         Git ref for a new worktree (origin/<branch>)
  --machine <id-or-name>      Machine to run on (alias --host)
  --section <id>              Sidebar section
  --visibility <visibility>   visible or hidden (a child inherits)
  --file <path>               Attach a file; an absolute path here is uploaded first (repeatable)
  --image <path>              Attach an image the same way (repeatable)
  --send-at <when>            ISO time (2026-08-25T09:00) or delay (30s, 10m, 2h)
JSON (--json): the created thread: {id, status, title, projectId, environmentId, …}

Usage: bb thread tell <id> [message] [options]
Send a message; a busy thread queues it
Aliases: message, send
Options:
  --message-file <path>      Read the message from a file (- reads stdin)
  --mode <mode>              steer (default), queue or auto
  --model <model>            Model ID
  --reasoning-level <level>  none, low, medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra, …
  --permission-mode <mode>   accept-edits, auto or full
  --file <path>              Attach a file; an absolute path here is uploaded first (repeatable)
  --image <path>             Attach an image the same way (repeatable)
  --send-at <when>           ISO time (2026-08-25T09:00) or delay (30s, 10m, 2h)
JSON (--json): {threadId, delivery: "sent" | "queued", queuedMessage?, mode}

Usage: bb thread wait <id> [options]
Block until a thread reaches a status (default idle) or event
Options:
  --status <status>           pending, idle, starting, active, stopping or error
  --event <type>              Wait for an event of this type instead
  --timeout <duration>        Seconds, or 90s, 20m, 4h (default 1200s)
  --poll-interval <duration>  Milliseconds, or 5s (default 250ms)
JSON (--json): {threadId, matched: true, target}; exit 2 on timeout, 3 on an invalid request, 4 when the thread cannot reach the status

Usage: bb thread show [id] [options]
Show a thread, its environment and its TODOs
Aliases: get, view, status
Options:
  --self  Target the current thread (BB_THREAD_ID)
JSON (--json): {thread, environment, pendingTodos} (thread fields are under .thread)

Usage: bb thread log [id] [options]
Print the timeline, or raw events as JSON
Aliases: messages, timeline
Options:
  --self             Target the current thread (BB_THREAD_ID)
  --format <format>  minimal (default), verbose or json
  --limit <count>    Events for json (default 100); turns otherwise (max 100)
  --after-seq <seq>  Events after this sequence (json only)
  --all              Page through the whole thread
JSON (--json): [{id, seq, type, createdAt, threadId, scope, data}] oldest first

Usage: bb thread output [id] [options]
Print the final assistant message of the last turn
Options:
  --self  Target the current thread (BB_THREAD_ID)
JSON (--json): {output}

Usage: bb thread list [options]
List threads
Options:
  --project <id>          Only this project
  --environment <id>      Only this environment
  --machine <id-or-name>  Only this machine (alias --host)
  --parent-thread <id>    Only children of this thread
  --section <id>          Only this section
  --unsectioned           Only threads outside sections
  --archived              Only archived threads
  --include-hidden        Include hidden threads
  --count                 Print only the number of matching threads
JSON (--json): [{id, projectId, title, status, parentThreadId, …}] (bare array)

Usage: bb thread update [id] [options]
Change title, parent, section, model or visibility
Options:
  --self                     Target the current thread (BB_THREAD_ID)
  --title <title>            New title
  --parent-thread <id>       New parent thread
  --clear-parent-thread      Remove the parent thread
  --section <id>             Move into a section
  --clear-section            Remove from its section
  --model <model>            Model for the next turn
  --reasoning-level <level>  Reasoning level for the next turn
  --visibility <visibility>  visible or hidden

Usage: bb thread stop [id] [options]
Stop work and release the agent runtime
Options:
  --self  Target the current thread (BB_THREAD_ID)

Usage: bb thread archive [id] [options]
Archive a thread and its children
Options:
  --self  Target the current thread (BB_THREAD_ID)

Usage: bb thread unarchive [id] [options]
Unarchive a thread
Options:
  --self  Target the current thread (BB_THREAD_ID)

Usage: bb thread compact [id] [options]
Compact the context of an idle thread
Options:
  --self  Target the current thread (BB_THREAD_ID)

Usage: bb thread clear [id] [options]
Clear the model context of an idle thread
Options:
  --self  Target the current thread (BB_THREAD_ID)

Usage: bb thread pin [id] [options]
Pin a thread
Options:
  --self  Target the current thread (BB_THREAD_ID)

Usage: bb thread unpin [id] [options]
Unpin a thread
Options:
  --self  Target the current thread (BB_THREAD_ID)

Usage: bb thread read [id] [options]
Mark a thread read
Options:
  --self  Target the current thread (BB_THREAD_ID)

Usage: bb thread unread [id] [options]
Mark a thread unread
Options:
  --self  Target the current thread (BB_THREAD_ID)

Usage: bb thread delete <id> [options]
Delete a thread permanently
Options:
  --yes                    Skip the confirmation prompt
  --confirm-child-threads  Also delete its child threads

Usage: bb thread search <query> [options]
Search thread titles and messages
Options:
  --limit <count>  Results per group

Usage: bb thread open [id] [path] [options]
Open a thread in the app, optionally with a file
Options:
  --line <number>      Line to focus
  --split <placement>  right, down, left, top or replace

Usage: bb thread interactions list [id] [options]
List approvals, questions and plugin forms
Options:
  --self  Target the current thread (BB_THREAD_ID)

Usage: bb thread interactions show <interactionId> [id] [options]
Show one interaction in full
Options:
  --self  Target the current thread (BB_THREAD_ID)

Usage: bb thread interactions resolve <interactionId> [id] [options]
Approve, deny or answer one
Options:
  --self                     Target the current thread (BB_THREAD_ID)
  --approve                  Approve a command, file change or tool use
  --deny                     Deny it
  --grant <scope>            Grant a permission request for the turn or the session
  --answer <question=value>  Choose an option of a question (repeatable)
  --text <question=text>     Answer a question in free text (repeatable)
  --value <json>             Answer a plugin form with a JSON value

Usage: bb thread queue list [id] [options]
List the queued messages of a thread
Options:
  --self  Target the current thread (BB_THREAD_ID)

Usage: bb thread queue send <threadId> <messageId> [options]
Send a queued message now
Options:
  --mode <mode>  auto (default) or steer

Usage: bb thread queue delete <threadId> <messageId> [options]
Delete a queued message

Usage: bb thread section list [options]
List sidebar sections

Usage: bb thread section create <name> [options]
Create a sidebar section

Usage: bb thread section rename <id> <name> [options]
Rename a sidebar section

Usage: bb thread section delete <id> [options]
Delete a section; its threads become unsectioned
Options:
  --yes  Skip the confirmation prompt

Usage: bb project list [options]
List projects
Options:
  --include-personal  Include the personal project
JSON (--json): [{id, kind, name, gitRemoteUrl, sources: [{id, hostId, path}]}]

Usage: bb project show <id> [options]
Show a project and its sources

Usage: bb project create [options]
Create a project from a directory on a machine
Options:
  --name <name>           Project name (required)
  --root <path>           Project directory (default: the current directory)
  --machine <id-or-name>  Machine holding it (default: this one) (alias --host)

Usage: bb project update <id> [options]
Rename a project
Options:
  --name <name>  New name

Usage: bb project delete <id> [options]
Delete a project and its threads
Options:
  --yes  Skip the confirmation prompt

Usage: bb project source add <projectId> [options]
Add the project's directory on another machine
Options:
  --path <path>           Directory of an existing checkout (required)
  --machine <id-or-name>  Machine holding it (default: this one) (alias --host)
  --default               Make it the default source

Usage: bb project source update <projectId> <sourceId> [options]
Change a source
Options:
  --path <path>  New directory
  --default      Make it the default source

Usage: bb project source delete <projectId> <sourceId> [options]
Remove a project source
Options:
  --yes  Skip the confirmation prompt

Usage: bb project attachment upload <id> [options]
Upload a file here as a prompt attachment
Options:
  --client-file <path>  File to upload (required)
  --filename <name>     Stored file name

Usage: bb env list [options]
List environments: the checkouts and worktrees threads run in
Options:
  --project <id>          Only this project
  --machine <id-or-name>  Only this machine (alias --host)
  --status <status>       ready or destroyed
  --limit <count>         At most this many, oldest first
JSON (--json): [{id, name, projectId, hostId, path, branchName, status}]

Usage: bb env show <id> [options]
Show an environment
Aliases: get

Usage: bb env status <id> [options]
Show the git state of an environment
Options:
  --merge-base-branch <branch>  Also compare with this branch

Usage: bb env commit <id> [options]
Commit every change in an environment

Usage: bb env update <id> [options]
Rename an environment or set its merge-base branch
Options:
  --name <name>                 Display name
  --clear-name                  Remove the display name
  --merge-base-branch <branch>  Branch that diffs compare against
  --clear-merge-base-branch     Use the default merge base again

Usage: bb env delete <id> [options]
Delete an environment that has no live threads
Options:
  --yes  Skip the confirmation prompt

Usage: bb machine list [options]
List machines, their owners and who may use them
JSON (--json): [{id, name, type, status, lifecycle, ownerUserId, sharing, usable, lastSeenAt}] (bare array)

Usage: bb machine show <machine> [options]
Show a machine, by ID or name

Usage: bb machine add [options]
Register a machine and print the command that joins it
Options:
  --name <name>  Machine name (default: its hostname)

Usage: bb machine reconnect <machine> [options]
Print a new join command for an offline machine

Usage: bb machine rename <machine> <name> [options]
Rename a machine

Usage: bb machine remove <machine> [options]
Revoke and remove a machine
Options:
  --yes  Skip the confirmation prompt

Usage: bb machine share <machine> [options]
Let every user run threads on a machine

Usage: bb machine unshare <machine> [options]
Keep a machine to its owner

Usage: bb machine env list [options]
List variables given to agents (values stay hidden)
Options:
  --project <id>  Variables of one project

Usage: bb machine env set <name> [options]
Set an agent variable; the value is read from stdin
Options:
  --project <id>  Only for this project
  --note <text>   What it is for

Usage: bb machine env unset <name> [options]
Remove an agent variable
Options:
  --project <id>  Only for this project

Usage: bb user list [options]
List the people who can sign in
JSON (--json): [{id, name, email, role, hasPassword, disabledAt, createdAt}] (bare array)

Usage: bb user invite [options]
Create an invite link for a new person
Options:
  --name <name>    Their name
  --email <email>  Their email address
  --role <role>    owner or member
JSON (--json): {id, name, email, role, createdByUserId, expiresAt, createdAt, url}

Usage: bb user invites [options]
List the invites nobody has accepted yet
JSON (--json): [{id, name, email, role, createdByUserId, expiresAt, createdAt}]

Usage: bb user revoke-invite <id> [options]
Revoke an invite

Usage: bb user sign-in-link [id] [options]
Print a one-time sign-in link (default: for yourself)
JSON (--json): {url, expiresAt, userId}

Usage: bb user role <id> <role> [options]
Make a user an owner or a member

Usage: bb user disable <id> [options]
Stop a user from signing in

Usage: bb user enable <id> [options]
Let a disabled user sign in again

Usage: bb provider list [options]
List providers usable on a machine
Options:
  --machine <id-or-name>  Ask this machine (alias --host)
  --environment <id>      Ask the machine of this environment
  --all                   Show the whole catalog, disabled providers included
JSON (--json): [{id, displayName, capabilities, …}] (bare array)

Usage: bb provider models [providerId] [options]
List the models of a provider
Options:
  --machine <id-or-name>  Ask this machine (alias --host)
  --environment <id>      Ask the machine of this environment
JSON (--json): [{id, model, displayName, isDefault, …}] (bare array)

Usage: bb provider enable <providerId> [options]
Enable a provider for new turns

Usage: bb provider disable <providerId> [options]
Disable a provider for new turns

Usage: bb terminal create [command...] [options]
Start a shell or a command
Aliases: start
Options:
  --thread <id>           Terminal of a thread (inside one: $BB_THREAD_ID)
  --environment <id>      Terminal of an environment
  --machine <id-or-name>  Terminal on a machine (alias --host)
  --cwd <path>            Working directory, with --machine
  --command <command>     Shell command to run instead of a login shell
  --title <title>         Terminal title
  --cols <n>              Columns (default 80)
  --rows <n>              Rows (default 24)
JSON (--json): the session: {id, title, status, exitCode, cols, rows, …}

Usage: bb terminal list [options]
List terminals in one scope
Options:
  --thread <id>           Terminal of a thread (inside one: $BB_THREAD_ID)
  --environment <id>      Terminal of an environment
  --machine <id-or-name>  Terminal on a machine (alias --host)
  --cwd <path>            Working directory, with --machine
JSON (--json): {sessions: [{id, title, status, exitCode, closeReason, cols, rows}]}

Usage: bb terminal output <terminalId> [options]
Print terminal scrollback
Aliases: read
Options:
  --since-seq <n>     Only chunks from this sequence
  --tail-bytes <n>    Only the latest N bytes
  --limit-chunks <n>  Only the latest N chunks
JSON (--json): {chunks: [{seq, dataBase64}], nextSeq, truncated, status, exitCode, closeReason}

Usage: bb terminal wait <terminalId> [options]
Wait for output or exit (exit 124 if it ends first)
Options:
  --contains <text>           Wait until the output contains this text
  --regex <pattern>           Wait until the output matches
  --exit                      Wait until the terminal exits
  --from-start                Search existing scrollback too
  --timeout <duration>        Seconds, or 90s, 20m (default 30s)
  --poll-interval <duration>  Milliseconds, or 2s (default 500ms)
  --tail-bytes <n>            Only the latest N bytes
  --limit-chunks <n>          Only the latest N chunks
JSON (--json): {terminalId, matched, nextSeq, exitCode}

Usage: bb terminal send <terminalId> [options]
Send input to a terminal
Options:
  --text <text>  Text to send
  --stdin        Send the bytes read from stdin
  --enter        Append a newline

Usage: bb terminal close <terminalId> [options]
Close a terminal
Aliases: stop
Options:
  --if-clean  Only if nobody typed into it

Usage: bb file read <path> [options]
Print a file from a machine
Options:
  --machine <id-or-name>  Machine holding the file (default: the server's) (alias --host)
  --root <path>           Refuse paths outside this directory

Usage: bb file write <path> [options]
Write a UTF-8 file on a machine
Options:
  --machine <id-or-name>    Machine holding the file (default: the server's) (alias --host)
  --content <text>          File content
  --stdin                   Read the content from stdin
  --root <path>             Refuse paths outside this directory
  --create-parents          Create missing parent directories
  --expected-sha256 <hash>  Only write when the current hash matches

Usage: bb file list <path> [options]
List files under a directory on a machine
Options:
  --machine <id-or-name>  Machine holding the directory (default: the server's) (alias --host)
  --query <query>         Fuzzy path filter
  --limit <count>         Maximum entries

Usage: bb settings show [options]
Print every setting as key = value

Usage: bb settings get <key> [options]
Print one setting

Usage: bb settings set <key> <value> [options]
Set a general setting, theme, keybinding.* or ui.*

Usage: bb settings reset <key> [options]
Restore one setting to its default

Usage: bb plugin list [options]
List plugins, their state and the commands they add
JSON (--json): {plugins: [{id, name, enabled, status, cliCommands, …}]}

Usage: bb plugin enable <id> [options]
Enable a plugin

Usage: bb plugin disable <id> [options]
Disable a plugin

Usage: bb plugin reload [id] [options]
Reload one plugin, or rediscover and reload all of them

Usage: bb plugin add <path> [options]
Load a plugin directory (adds it to <dataDir>/config.json)

Usage: bb plugin remove <path> [options]
Stop loading a plugin directory
Options:
  --yes  Skip the confirmation prompt

Usage: bb server [options]
Run the bb server in the foreground

Usage: bb server status [options]
Check that the server answers and show its data directory

Usage: bb import-legacy [options]
Copy projects, sections, settings and threads from an old bb
Options:
  --from <dir>       Data directory of the original install; it is only read
  --threads <which>  active (unarchived threads and their families), all, none
  --dry-run          Only count what each --threads choice would import
JSON (--json): {dryRun, dataDir, choices, counts: {<table>: {imported, skipped}}, …}

Usage: bb runner join <blob> [options]
Enrol this machine with the command bb machine add printed
Options:
  --header <name=value>              Header sent on every request to the server (repeatable)
  --reuse-connect-credential [path]  Reuse an old install's connect credential
  --data-dir <dir>                   Where to keep runner.json
  --name <name>                      Machine name (default: the hostname)

Usage: bb runner run [options]
Run this machine's runner in the foreground
Options:
  --data-dir <dir>  Directory that bb runner join wrote

Every command takes --json. With --json a failure prints {"ok": false, "error": {code, message, hint?}} on stdout, the readable message on stderr, and exits non-zero.
